For each admitted material constitution $c$, the model adopts a finite scalar function

$$S_c:D_c\longrightarrow\mathbb R\ \text{with values measured in }\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}},$$

on the equilibrium state domain $D_c$ of [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]]. This framework treats $S_c$ as primitive constitutive data: its existence and form are assumed, not derived from the word entropy, statistical mechanics, or experimental evidence.

On every specified convex region $C\subseteq D_c$ in the dimensionless coordinates of [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]], $S_c$ is continuous and concave, meaning that for all $x,y\in C$ and every $\alpha\in[0,1]$ ([[def-interval]]),

$$S_c((1-\alpha)x+\alpha y)\ge (1-\alpha)S_c(x)+\alpha S_c(y).$$

The domain assumptions are local to the material and region named; no unlisted coordinate tuple is presumed physically realizable. The input of $S_c$ is the represented state $\pi_c(e)$; when the function is written using physical coordinates $(U,V,n_1,\ldots,n_r)$, those coordinates mean the SI values whose dimensionless numerical tuple is $\pi_c(e)$. For independent separated macroscopic systems $A,B$ admitted by [[post-td-bulk-additivity]], entropy is additive under that postulate's composition map $\kappa_{AB}$:

$$S_{A\sqcup B}(\kappa_{AB}(x_A,x_B))=S_A(x_A)+S_B(x_B).$$

On each separately designated open, single-phase chart in the physical coordinates $(U,V,n_1,\ldots,n_r)$, assume the numerical representative of $S_c$ is $C^2$ in the sense of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]: its first and second coordinate partial derivatives exist and are continuous. The partial derivative $S_U$ at fixed $V,n_1,\ldots,n_r$ is the ordinary partial derivative in the $U$ coordinate, as in [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]], and is assumed finite and strictly positive. The numerical chart input uses $\hat U=U/(1\,\mathrm J)$; consequently $S_U=(1\,\mathrm J)^{-1}\partial S_c/\partial\hat U$ and has units $\mathrm{K^{-1}}$. The other physical coordinates are similarly represented using the fixed SI units of [[def-td-si-quantities]]. No differentiability, strict concavity, or positive $S_U$ is asserted outside those charts. This item does not itself define a thermometer calibration or claim a temperature law.

For the tagged bulk family with scaling maps $\delta_\lambda$ and domains $B_{c,\lambda}$ from [[post-td-bulk-additivity]], also adopt, for every admitted $\lambda>0$ and $x\in B_{c,\lambda}$,

$$S_{c^{(\lambda)}}(\delta_\lambda x)=\lambda S_c(x).$$

This is a bulk homogeneity assumption for tagged scaled systems, not exact finite-size scaling for every body. Lieb–Yngvason develop a different accessibility-based route in which entropy is represented from additional operational hypotheses; this framework does not claim that their derivation proves the present primitive entropy postulate.

A material constitution $c$ specifies a finite ordered list of named species $(\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_r)$, with $r\in\mathbb N$ ([[def-natural-numbers]]) and $r\ge1$, and the model parameters that identify the material. An equilibrium-preparation label in the set $E_c$ selects a single macrostate that the model designates as an equilibrium state for constitution $c$. The equilibrium designation is primitive model input here; it is not a dynamical equilibration theorem or a global-stability claim. For each admitted preparation, its mechanical model supplies a positive total mass and a defined center-of-mass velocity as in [[def-td-galilean-rest-frame]], so the allowed boost can select a center-of-mass rest chart in which its internal energy is recorded. A preparation for which these mechanical data are unavailable lies outside this framework. A statistical preparation that instead supplies a normalized probability measure on a declared measurable space is as in [[def-probability-measure]] and belongs to a separate statistical branch; it is an element of $E_c$ only if that model also assigns it a single equilibrium macrostate.

Each $e\in E_c$ is assigned a unique coordinate tuple $(U,V,n_1,\ldots,n_r)$, where $U$ is the adopted internal-energy coordinate in joules as in [[def-td-galilean-rest-frame]], $V>0$ is volume in cubic metres, and each $n_j>0$ is an amount in moles; the SI unit assignments are those of [[def-td-si-quantities]]. These are real-valued mole amounts in the bulk continuous chart, not integer particle counts. Define the dimensionless numerical coordinates $\hat U=U/(1\,\mathrm J)$, $\hat V=V/(1\,\mathrm{m^3})$, and $\hat n_j=n_j/(1\,\mathrm{mol})$. The representation map $\pi_c:E_c\to\mathbb R^{r+2}$ is a function as in [[def-function-space]], sends $e$ to $(\hat U,\hat V,\hat n_1,\ldots,\hat n_r)$, and the equilibrium state domain is its image $D_c:=\pi_c(E_c)\subseteq\mathbb R^{r+2}$ using inclusion as in [[def-subset-and-proper-subset]]. For $x=(\hat U,\hat V,\hat n_1,\ldots,\hat n_r)\in D_c$, write $U_c(x):=\hat U\,\mathrm J$, $V_c(x):=\hat V\,\mathrm{m^3}$, and $n_{c,j}(x):=\hat n_j\,\mathrm{mol}$ for its dimensioned coordinates. Preparation labels with the same coordinate tuple represent the same thermodynamic state in this framework. Statistical preparations that specify a probability law belong to a separate branch and are not used in this state-domain definition.

For fixed $n=(n_1,\ldots,n_r)$ in a chart used by the model, write $\Gamma_{c,n}=\{(\hat U,\hat V):(\hat U,\hat V,\hat n)\in D_c\}\subseteq\mathbb R^2$, with inclusion notation as in [[def-subset-and-proper-subset]]. This designated slice is a specified nonempty open convex subset. With the dimensionless Euclidean norm $\|\cdot\|_2$ of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]] (a norm by [[thm-cauchy-schwarz-and-the-euclidean-norm]]), openness means that every $z\in\Gamma_{c,n}$ has some $\epsilon>0$ for which $\{w\in\mathbb R^2:\|w-z\|_2<\epsilon\}\subseteq\Gamma_{c,n}$. Convexity means that $(1-t)z_0+tz_1\in\Gamma_{c,n}$ whenever $z_0,z_1\in\Gamma_{c,n}$ and $t\in[0,1]$, as in [[def-convex-subset-of-euclidean-space]]. Both properties are assumptions about the particular slice, not conclusions about every $D_c$; no coordinate tuple is presumed physically realizable merely because it lies in an ambient Euclidean space. A zero amount for an absent species belongs only to a separately specified boundary domain and is not in this positive-mole chart.

In a simple-compressible chart, volume $V$ is the only mechanical coordinate in the equilibrium representation; composition changes, fields, polarization, surface terms, and other mechanical coordinates require a separately declared state domain and exchange rules. No pressure or reversible-work formula follows from this definition.

For this nonrelativistic framework, a Newtonian event-coordinate domain is the Cartesian product $I\times\mathbb R^3$ ([[def-cartesian-product]]), where $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ is an open time interval as in [[def-interval]], measured in seconds, and $\mathbb R^3$ has the Euclidean inner product and norm of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]] (the norm properties follow from [[thm-cauchy-schwarz-and-the-euclidean-norm]]); lengths are measured in metres as in [[def-td-si-quantities]]. $$t'=t+\tau,\qquad \mathbf x'=R\mathbf x+\mathbf a-\mathbf b t,$$

In the coordinate formula, $(R\mathbf x)_i:=\sum_{k<3}R_{ik}x_k$ for $i<3$. Thus time is absolute in this model and no Lorentzian structure is used. Here “frame” means this coordinate chart, not an observer congruence or a basis/tetrad field.

For a finite point-mass representation with $N\in\mathbb N$ ([[def-natural-numbers]]), $N\ge1$, masses $m_i>0$ in kg at positions $\mathbf x_i\in\mathbb R^3$ in metres for $i<N$, assume $M:=\sum_{i<N}m_i>0$ ([[def-finite-sum]]) and define the center-of-mass coordinates by $X_{\mathrm{cm},j}:=M^{-1}\sum_{i<N}m_i x_{i,j}$ for $j<3$; these three real coordinates form $\mathbf X_{\mathrm{cm}}$. The masses are invariant under the allowed chart changes. Other mechanical models must supply their total mass and center-of-mass map; this thermodynamic item does not construct those quantities for a continuum or field model. Every admitted mechanical model must also supply center-of-mass maps and velocities that transform under the displayed Galilean chart changes by $\mathbf X'_{\mathrm{cm}}(t')=R\mathbf X_{\mathrm{cm}}(t)+\mathbf a-\mathbf b t$ and $\mathbf v'_{\mathrm{cm}}=R\mathbf v_{\mathrm{cm}}-\mathbf b$, where $t'=t+\tau$; these are kinematic compatibility conditions, not dynamical theorems about arbitrary mechanical models. When the model supplies a center-of-mass position $\mathbf X_{\mathrm{cm}}:I\to\mathbb R^3$ ([[def-function-space]]), its velocity at a time $t$ is the componentwise limit $\mathbf v_{\mathrm{cm}}(t)=\lim_{h\to0}(\mathbf X_{\mathrm{cm}}(t+h)-\mathbf X_{\mathrm{cm}}(t))/h$ through $H_t:=\{h\in\mathbb R:t+h\in I,\ h\ne0\}$ ([[def-function-limit]]), when that limit exists. In this framework $U$ denotes the scalar internal-energy coordinate evaluated in the center-of-mass rest frame. Bulk translational kinetic energy and any separately tracked external-field potential energy are excluded from $U$. The model treats $U$ as invariant between rest charts that differ only by spatial translation or orthogonal orientation, and fixes its numerical zero, including any retained or subtracted constituent rest-energy offsets, consistently across the composition changes it admits. This is a nonrelativistic modeling convention, not a derived energy-transformation law.

Let $\Omega\subseteq D_c$ be a specified open, single-phase chart in physical SI coordinates $(U,V,n_1,\ldots,n_r)$, with $U$ evaluated in the center-of-mass rest frame of [[def-td-galilean-rest-frame]]. On $\Omega$, use the finite $C^2$ entropy function $S_c$ and the strict positivity $S_{c,U}>0$ adopted by [[post-td-concave-fundamental-entropy]]. Here $C^2$ means that all coordinate partial derivatives through order two exist and are continuous ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]). A coordinate partial such as $S_{c,U}$ is the ordinary derivative in that coordinate direction while every other physical coordinate is held fixed, as in [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]].

Define the **absolute thermodynamic temperature**, **entropic pressure**, and **molar chemical potential** of species $j$ by

$$T_c:=\frac{1}{S_{c,U}},\qquad p_c:=T_cS_{c,V},\qquad \mu_{c,j}:=-T_cS_{c,n_j}.$$

The entropy unit is $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, the energy $U$ is in joules, $V$ is in cubic metres, and $n_j$ is in moles ([[def-td-si-quantities]]). Thus $S_{c,U}$ has units $\mathrm{K^{-1}}$, $T_c$ is finite and positive in kelvins, $S_{c,V}$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-3}}$ and $p_c$ has units pascals, and $S_{c,n_j}$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,mol^{-1}}$ and $\mu_{c,j}$ has units $\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}}$. If a microscopic model instead uses a dimensionless particle count $N_j=N_{\!A}n_j$, the corresponding per-particle chemical potential is $\mu_{c,j}/N_{\!A}$ joules, with the exact SI Avogadro constant from [[def-td-si-quantities]].

These are scalar state functions of the stated rest-frame equilibrium chart. The pressure in this definition is a derivative-defined conjugate; identifying it with force per area requires a separate adopted mechanical coupling. Neither an empirical thermometer calibration nor any equation of state is supplied by this definition.

Let $f:U\to V\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be totally differentiable at $a\in U$ and let $g:V\to\mathbb R^p$ be totally differentiable at $f(a)$. Then $g\circ f$ is totally differentiable at $a$ and

$$D(g\circ f)(a)=Dg(f(a))\circ Df(a).$$

Let $1\le q\le n$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, and let $F:U\to\mathbb R^q$ be $C^1$ in the sense of [[def-c-one-map-and-local-inverse]]. Suppose $F(x_*)=0$ and some $q\times q$ minor of the derivative matrix $DF(x_*)$ is invertible. This nonsingular-minor hypothesis is the explicit full-row-rank condition used here. If $q<n$, then after permuting coordinates $x=(u,v)\in\mathbb R^{n-q}\times\mathbb R^q$, there are open neighborhoods $P$ of $u_*$ and $Q$ of $v_*$ and a unique $C^1$ map $\varphi:P\to Q$ such that

$$F(u,v)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad v=\varphi(u)\qquad((u,v)\in P\times Q).$$

Its derivative is

$$D\varphi(u)=-D_vF(u,\varphi(u))^{-1}D_uF(u,\varphi(u)).$$

Thus the local zero set is a graph over $n-q$ free coordinates. If $q=n$, the zero is locally isolated, so the local graph dimension is zero. Here “local graph dimension $k$” means a local graph parameterized by an open subset of $\mathbb R^k$, with a singleton counted as dimension zero.

Let $\mathcal F$ be the explicitly declared feasible endpoint set of an isolated compound whose constituents are independent separated macroscopic systems, as defined in [[def-td-isolated-compound-feasible-set]]. For this route, adopt the physical criterion that any endpoint tuple the model classifies as a stable equilibrium under these fixed totals, retained partitions, and permitted exchanges satisfies

$$S_{\mathrm{tot}}(x^{\mathrm{eq}})=\max_{x\in\mathcal F}S_{\mathrm{tot}}(x),\qquad S_{\mathrm{tot}}(x):=\sum_{i=1}^{m}S_{c_i}(x_i),$$

Here $\max$ means that $x^{\mathrm{eq}}\in\mathcal F$ and $S_{\mathrm{tot}}(x^{\mathrm{eq}})\ge S_{\mathrm{tot}}(x)$ for every $x\in\mathcal F$, using maximum in the sense of [[def-max-min]]. The finite sum is as in [[def-finite-sum]], and the summands are those of the separated macroscopic constituents under [[post-td-concave-fundamental-entropy]]. Whenever the stable-equilibrium label is used, attainment is assumed: at least one maximizing endpoint lies in $\mathcal F$. If $\mathcal F$ is empty or the entropy supremum is not attained, this item supplies no equilibrium state.

“Global” refers to every endpoint in this exact $\mathcal F$, not just nearby states, states reachable by a restricted short-time dynamics, or states on a selected branch. A local maximum that is not global, or a long-lived preparation trapped by kinetic barriers, is not declared stable equilibrium by this postulate. No uniqueness or relaxation dynamics is assumed.

Fix a finite list of named subsystems $s_1,\ldots,s_m$, where $m\in\mathbb N$ and $m\ge1$ ([[def-natural-numbers]]), each having its own equilibrium state domain $D_{c_i}$ as defined in [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]]. Their separated endpoint state space is the Cartesian product ([[def-cartesian-product]])

$$\mathcal D:=D_{c_1}\times\cdots\times D_{c_m}.$$

An **isolated compound** is the system consisting of those subsystems and any named auxiliaries or work devices included inside a declared outer boundary, with no matter or energy transfer across that outer boundary during the admitted process, in the sense of [[def-td-system-and-permitted-exchanges]]. Transfers between constituents are internal to the compound. Its total energy and other extensive coordinates use the composition convention of [[post-td-bulk-additivity]]. The additive entropy sum applies only when the constituent split is admitted by [[post-td-concave-fundamental-entropy]] as a collection of independent separated macroscopic systems; an interacting compound outside that scope needs its own total-entropy model.

For specified totals and retained barriers, an **equilibrium feasible set** is the model-declared subset $\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal D$ of endpoint tuples satisfying those totals and exactly the exchange permissions in the declared protocol. Totals are imposed on the dimensioned coordinate maps $U_c,V_c,n_{c,j}$ of [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]], not by treating the dimensionless numerical coordinates as quantities with units. For example, if two constituents are in thermal contact through [[def-td-thermal-contact-constraints]] while their volumes and mole amounts remain fixed, $\mathcal F$ consists of the energy partitions $(x_A,x_B)$ with the prescribed total energy and those fixed volumes and amounts. Allowing volume or species exchange changes $\mathcal F$ only when the protocol explicitly permits that exchange; retained walls keep the corresponding coordinates fixed.

The set $\mathcal F$ may be empty, noncompact, or otherwise fail to contain an entropy-maximizing state. This definition imposes no existence, compactness, convexity, uniqueness, or attainment assumption.

For each admitted material constitution $c$, the model adopts a finite scalar function

$$S_c:D_c\longrightarrow\mathbb R\ \text{with values measured in }\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}},$$

on the equilibrium state domain $D_c$ of [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]]. This framework treats $S_c$ as primitive constitutive data: its existence and form are assumed, not derived from the word entropy, statistical mechanics, or experimental evidence.

On every specified convex region $C\subseteq D_c$ in the dimensionless coordinates of [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]], $S_c$ is continuous and concave, meaning that for all $x,y\in C$ and every $\alpha\in[0,1]$ ([[def-interval]]),

$$S_c((1-\alpha)x+\alpha y)\ge (1-\alpha)S_c(x)+\alpha S_c(y).$$

The domain assumptions are local to the material and region named; no unlisted coordinate tuple is presumed physically realizable. The input of $S_c$ is the represented state $\pi_c(e)$; when the function is written using physical coordinates $(U,V,n_1,\ldots,n_r)$, those coordinates mean the SI values whose dimensionless numerical tuple is $\pi_c(e)$. For independent separated macroscopic systems $A,B$ admitted by [[post-td-bulk-additivity]], entropy is additive under that postulate's composition map $\kappa_{AB}$:

$$S_{A\sqcup B}(\kappa_{AB}(x_A,x_B))=S_A(x_A)+S_B(x_B).$$

On each separately designated open, single-phase chart in the physical coordinates $(U,V,n_1,\ldots,n_r)$, assume the numerical representative of $S_c$ is $C^2$ in the sense of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]: its first and second coordinate partial derivatives exist and are continuous. The partial derivative $S_U$ at fixed $V,n_1,\ldots,n_r$ is the ordinary partial derivative in the $U$ coordinate, as in [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]], and is assumed finite and strictly positive. The numerical chart input uses $\hat U=U/(1\,\mathrm J)$; consequently $S_U=(1\,\mathrm J)^{-1}\partial S_c/\partial\hat U$ and has units $\mathrm{K^{-1}}$. The other physical coordinates are similarly represented using the fixed SI units of [[def-td-si-quantities]]. No differentiability, strict concavity, or positive $S_U$ is asserted outside those charts. This item does not itself define a thermometer calibration or claim a temperature law.

For the tagged bulk family with scaling maps $\delta_\lambda$ and domains $B_{c,\lambda}$ from [[post-td-bulk-additivity]], also adopt, for every admitted $\lambda>0$ and $x\in B_{c,\lambda}$,

$$S_{c^{(\lambda)}}(\delta_\lambda x)=\lambda S_c(x).$$

This is a bulk homogeneity assumption for tagged scaled systems, not exact finite-size scaling for every body. Lieb–Yngvason develop a different accessibility-based route in which entropy is represented from additional operational hypotheses; this framework does not claim that their derivation proves the present primitive entropy postulate.

Let $A$ and $B$ be two named subsystems with disjoint physical regions as in [[def-td-system-and-permitted-exchanges]], combined as a compound system $A\sqcup B$ inside a declared outer boundary. The model's admitted separated pairs form a specified subset $\mathcal C_{AB}\subseteq D_A\times D_B$ using [[def-subset-and-proper-subset]] and [[def-cartesian-product]]. For every pair $(x_A,x_B)\in\mathcal C_{AB}$, the composition map $\kappa_{AB}:\mathcal C_{AB}\to D_{A\sqcup B}$ is a function ([[def-function-space]]) adopted so the dimensioned coordinates of its output satisfy
$$U_{A\sqcup B}(\kappa_{AB}(x_A,x_B))=U_A(x_A)+U_B(x_B),\qquad V_{A\sqcup B}(\kappa_{AB}(x_A,x_B))=V_A(x_A)+V_B(x_B),\qquad n_{A\sqcup B,j}(\kappa_{AB}(x_A,x_B))=n_{A,j}(x_A)+n_{B,j}(x_B).$$
Here each coordinate function is the dimensioned map of [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]] for its material constitution, with SI units as in [[def-td-si-quantities]].

Here “extensive coordinates” means precisely the named coordinates declared additive by this postulate. Amount coordinates are aligned by species label; when a species is absent from one subsystem, its zero amount is in a separately declared composition boundary, not the positive-mole chart of [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]]. This is an idealized composition rule: cross-interface and long-range interaction energy is omitted from $U_{A\sqcup B}$, rather than asserted to vanish in nature. The postulate does not assert that every pair of subsystem states is physically admissible.

The framework's bulk family is a tagged family of material types. For each dimensionless scale $\lambda>0$ the model may designate a tag $c^{(\lambda)}$ and a subset $B_{c,\lambda}\subseteq D_c$ of states admitting a scaled copy, with inclusion as in [[def-subset-and-proper-subset]]. For $x=(\hat U,\hat V,\hat n_1,\ldots,\hat n_r)\in B_{c,\lambda}$, the scaling map is the function $\delta_\lambda:B_{c,\lambda}\to D_{c^{(\lambda)}}$ ([[def-function-space]]) given by $\delta_\lambda(x)=(\lambda\hat U,\lambda\hat V,\lambda\hat n_1,\ldots,\lambda\hat n_r)$. This postulate specifies the coordinate scaling model and energy additivity only; it does not postulate entropy additivity or exact scaling for every finite physical body.

This is an adopted physical composition rule, not a deduction from SI units or from the mathematics of Cartesian products.

For each material constitution $c$, let $D_c$ be the equilibrium state domain from [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]]. A **thermal-contact family** is a model-declared set $\mathcal T$ of tagged pairs $(c,x)$ with $x\in D_c$. A **thermal-contact protocol** for two states $x,y\in\mathcal T$ is an admitted preparation of their compound system in which the two constituents are separated by a declared diathermal contact: matter transfer and mechanical or composition work across that contact are forbidden, while the protocol permits thermal energy transfer between the constituents. The compound's external boundary and all retained constraints are specified as in [[def-td-system-and-permitted-exchanges]] and [[def-td-process-and-protocol]].

The pair is in **thermal contact equilibrium**, written $x\sim_T y$, when the admitted contact preparation leaves both constituent coordinates unchanged, is an equilibrium preparation, and permits no net heat transfer between them. The relation $\sim_T$ is defined only on the stated family $\mathcal T$ and for the declared contact protocols. This definition does not assert that $\sim_T$ is reflexive, symmetric, or transitive, and it does not assign a real-valued temperature to its equivalence classes.

Fix a material constitution $c$ and its equilibrium state domain $D_c$ from [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]]. Let $\Omega\subseteq D_c$ be a specified open, single-phase chart in physical SI coordinates $(U,V,n_1,\ldots,n_r)$, with $U$ evaluated in the center-of-mass rest frame of [[def-td-galilean-rest-frame]]. On $\Omega$, use the finite $C^2$ entropy function $S_c$ and the strict positivity $S_{c,U}>0$ adopted by [[post-td-concave-fundamental-entropy]]. Here $C^2$ means that all coordinate partial derivatives through order two exist and are continuous ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]). A coordinate partial such as $S_{c,U}$ is the ordinary derivative in that coordinate direction while every other physical coordinate is held fixed, as in [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]].

Define the **absolute thermodynamic temperature**, **entropic pressure**, and **molar chemical potential** of species $j$ by

$$T_c:=\frac{1}{S_{c,U}},\qquad p_c:=T_cS_{c,V},\qquad \mu_{c,j}:=-T_cS_{c,n_j}.$$

The entropy unit is $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, the energy $U$ is in joules, $V$ is in cubic metres, and $n_j$ is in moles ([[def-td-si-quantities]]). Thus $S_{c,U}$ has units $\mathrm{K^{-1}}$, $T_c$ is finite and positive in kelvins, $S_{c,V}$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-3}}$ and $p_c$ has units pascals, and $S_{c,n_j}$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,mol^{-1}}$ and $\mu_{c,j}$ has units $\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}}$. If a microscopic model instead uses a dimensionless particle count $N_j=N_{\!A}n_j$, the corresponding per-particle chemical potential is $\mu_{c,j}/N_{\!A}$ joules, with the exact SI Avogadro constant from [[def-td-si-quantities]].

These are scalar state functions of the stated rest-frame equilibrium chart. The pressure in this definition is a derivative-defined conjugate; identifying it with force per area requires a separate adopted mechanical coupling. Neither an empirical thermometer calibration nor any equation of state is supplied by this definition.

This framework uses the modern International System of Units (SI). A scalar quantity has a real numerical value with the stated unit; a vector quantity has a value in the stated real coordinate space with the stated component unit. The numerical coordinates used elsewhere on this page are divided by their displayed SI units before they are placed in a Euclidean coordinate space.

The model's energy coordinate $U$ and its process-transfer values $Q$ and $W_{\mathrm{on}}$ are scalar energies measured in joules (J). Volume $V$ is a scalar measured in cubic metres (m³); amount of substance $n_j$ for species $j$ is a scalar measured in moles (mol); and a particle count $N_j$, when separately used in a microscopic model, is dimensionless. Time $t$ is measured in seconds (s), mass $M$ in kilograms (kg), and a translational velocity $\mathbf v_{\mathrm{cm}}$ is a vector in $\mathbb R^3$ with components measured in metres per second (m/s). The physical meanings of $U,Q,W_{\mathrm{on}}$ are fixed by the state and process definitions, not by their units alone.

The relevant exact SI relations are

$$1\,\mathrm J=1\,\mathrm{kg\,m^2\,s^{-2}},\qquad 1\,\mathrm N=1\,\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-2}},\qquad 1\,\mathrm{Pa}=1\,\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}.$$

The kelvin (K) is the SI unit of thermodynamic temperature. The Boltzmann constant has the exact defining value $k_{\mathrm B}=1.380649\times10^{-23}\,\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$. The mole is the SI unit of amount of substance; the Avogadro constant has the exact defining value $N_{\mathrm A}=6.02214076\times10^{23}\,\mathrm{mol^{-1}}$. When a model uses particle counts, $n_j=N_j/N_{\mathrm A}$. The molar gas constant is derived as $R=N_{\mathrm A}k_{\mathrm B}=8.31446261815324\,\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$. This framework does not set $k_{\mathrm B}=1$. These SI definitions do not themselves introduce a thermodynamic temperature state function or entropy function.

Within the macroscopic framework, $(U,V,n_j)$ are adopted state coordinates. A quantity's status as primitive in this model is separate from whether its SI unit is a base or derived unit.

For a simple-compressible system whose only admitted mechanical equilibrium coordinate is volume, adopt the following piston coupling. The boundary is a planar piston with constant area $A>0$ in $\mathrm{m^2}$ and outward displacement coordinate $\ell$ in metres; increasing $\ell$ increases the enclosed volume by $dV=A\,d\ell$. Define the positive mechanical pressure $p_{\mathrm{mech}}$ as the outward normal force exerted by the system on the piston divided by $A$, so $p_{\mathrm{mech}}$ is in pascals. When the system is in quasistatic frictionless mechanical equilibrium with this piston, adopt the identification

$$p_{\mathrm{mech}}=p_c,$$

where $p_c$ is the entropic pressure of [[def-td-temperature-pressure-chemical-potential]]. With $W_{\mathrm{on}}$ positive for work done on the system, the same coupling assigns the incremental mechanical work

$$\delta W_{\mathrm{on}}=-p_{\mathrm{mech}}A\,d\ell=-p_c\,dV.$$

The sign agrees with [[def-td-process-and-protocol]]: compression has $dV<0$ and positive work on the system. This is an adopted, regime-limited physical assumption, not a deduction from the entropy derivative or from the first-law balance [[post-td-first-law-energy]]. It makes no claim for friction, nonquasistatic processes, changing piston area, shear, surface forces, fields, composition transfer, or other generalized coordinates.

Let $f:U\to V\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be totally differentiable at $a\in U$ and let $g:V\to\mathbb R^p$ be totally differentiable at $f(a)$. Then $g\circ f$ is totally differentiable at $a$ and

$$D(g\circ f)(a)=Dg(f(a))\circ Df(a).$$

For $t>0$, $(g(t)-g(0))/t\le0$; for $t<0$, the same quotient is $\ge0$. Its derivative exists by [F2], so the two one-sided limits force $g'(0)=0$. Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be open and convex, let $A:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^k$ be linear, let $b\in\mathbb R^k$, and let $x_*\in U$ satisfy $Ax_*=b$. Put $T=\ker A$. Assume $f:U\to\mathbb R$ is differentiable and has second directional derivatives represented by a continuous matrix field: there is a continuous map $H:U\to\mathbb R^{d\times d}$ with symmetric values, and for every $x\in U$ and $h\in\mathbb R^d$,

$$\left.\frac{d^2}{dt^2}f(x+th)\right|_{t=0}=Q_x(h):=h^{\mathsf T}H(x)h.$$

Assume stationarity $Df(x_*)h=0$ for every $h\in T$. If $Q_{x_*}(h_0)<0$ for some $h_0\in T$, then $x_*$ is not a local minimum of $f$ on $\{x\in U:Ax=b\}$. If $Q_{x_*}(h)>0$ for every nonzero $h\in T$, then $x_*$ is a strict local minimum on that feasible slice. If $T=\{0\}$, the latter conclusion holds because $x_*$ is the only feasible point.

Fix a material constitution $c$ and its equilibrium state domain $D_c$ from [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]]. Let $\Omega\subseteq D_c$ be a specified open, single-phase chart in physical SI coordinates $(U,V,n_1,\ldots,n_r)$, with $U$ evaluated in the center-of-mass rest frame of [[def-td-galilean-rest-frame]]. On $\Omega$, use the finite $C^2$ entropy function $S_c$ and the strict positivity $S_{c,U}>0$ adopted by [[post-td-concave-fundamental-entropy]]. Here $C^2$ means that all coordinate partial derivatives through order two exist and are continuous ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]). A coordinate partial such as $S_{c,U}$ is the ordinary derivative in that coordinate direction while every other physical coordinate is held fixed, as in [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]].

Define the **absolute thermodynamic temperature**, **entropic pressure**, and **molar chemical potential** of species $j$ by

$$T_c:=\frac{1}{S_{c,U}},\qquad p_c:=T_cS_{c,V},\qquad \mu_{c,j}:=-T_cS_{c,n_j}.$$

The entropy unit is $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, the energy $U$ is in joules, $V$ is in cubic metres, and $n_j$ is in moles ([[def-td-si-quantities]]). Thus $S_{c,U}$ has units $\mathrm{K^{-1}}$, $T_c$ is finite and positive in kelvins, $S_{c,V}$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-3}}$ and $p_c$ has units pascals, and $S_{c,n_j}$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,mol^{-1}}$ and $\mu_{c,j}$ has units $\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}}$. If a microscopic model instead uses a dimensionless particle count $N_j=N_{\!A}n_j$, the corresponding per-particle chemical potential is $\mu_{c,j}/N_{\!A}$ joules, with the exact SI Avogadro constant from [[def-td-si-quantities]].

These are scalar state functions of the stated rest-frame equilibrium chart. The pressure in this definition is a derivative-defined conjugate; identifying it with force per area requires a separate adopted mechanical coupling. Neither an empirical thermometer calibration nor any equation of state is supplied by this definition.

Fix a constitution $c$ and a smooth physical-coordinate chart in $D_c$ from [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]], with fixed amounts $n=(n_1,\ldots,n_r)$ and $T,p$ as in [[def-td-temperature-pressure-chemical-potential]]. A **valid response chart** is an open neighborhood on which the relevant independent coordinates used below have a $C^1$ inverse to the physical $(U,V)$ coordinates; a $C^1$ diffeomorphism has a $C^1$ inverse on open neighborhoods by [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]. The existence of such a chart is a hypothesis for a response derivative, not a consequence of this definition. The derivatives use the indicated natural variables and hold all other listed coordinates fixed.

The **constant-volume heat capacity** and **constant-pressure heat capacity** of the whole system are, where the derivatives exist and are finite,

$$C_V:=\left(\frac{\partial U}{\partial T}\right)_{V,n},\qquad H:=U+pV,\qquad C_p:=\left(\frac{\partial H}{\partial T}\right)_{p,n}.$$

Here $H$ is the enthalpy in joules; both heat capacities are in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, not per mole. The **isothermal compressibility** and **isobaric thermal expansion coefficient** are

$$\kappa_T:=-\frac{1}{V}\left(\frac{\partial V}{\partial p}\right)_{T,n},\qquad \alpha_p:=\frac{1}{V}\left(\frac{\partial V}{\partial T}\right)_{p,n}.$$

Since $V>0$ and the coordinates use SI units ([[def-td-si-quantities]]), $\kappa_T$ has units $\mathrm{Pa^{-1}}$ and $\alpha_p$ has units $\mathrm{K^{-1}}$. This definition asserts no sign for any response, no identity among them, and no finite value at a critical or otherwise singular chart.

For $x>0$, define $\log x$ to be the unique real $y$ such that $\exp(y)=x$. This is well-defined because [[cor-exponential-is-a-bijection-onto-positive-reals]] states that $\exp:\mathbb R\to(0,\infty)$ is a bijection.

Thus $\log:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ is the inverse function of $\exp$. In particular, $\log(\exp y)=y$ for every $y\in\mathbb R$ and $\exp(\log x)=x$ for every $x>0$.

For $x>0$, $\log$ is differentiable and
$$\log'(x)=\frac1x,\qquad \log x=\int_1^x\frac{dt}{t}.$$

derivations.claim: The positive ratios in the stipulated entropy are in the domain of [F2]. By [L1], $S_U=a/U$ and $S_V=b/V$. Substitution in [A1] gives $T=U/a>0$ and $p=bU/(aV)=bT/V$. The entropy Hessian is diagonal with entries $-a/U^2$ and $-b/V^2$, so its quadratic form is nonpositive; this chart is concave.

Solving $T=U/a$ gives $U=aT$, hence $C_V=(\partial U/\partial T)_{V,n}=a$. Solving $p=bT/V$ gives $V=bT/p$, so $(\partial V/\partial p)_{T,n}=-bT/p^2$ and $(\partial V/\partial T)_{p,n}=b/p$. With $V=bT/p$, [F1] yields $\kappa_T=1/p$ and $\alpha_p=1/T$. These inverses are smooth for $T,p>0$.

The enthalpy in [F1] is $H=U+pV=aT+bT=(a+b)T$, so $C_p=(\partial H/\partial T)_{p,n}=a+b$. All displayed units are consistent: $C_V,C_p$ are $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, $\kappa_T$ is $\mathrm{Pa^{-1}}$, and $\alpha_p$ is $\mathrm{K^{-1}}$.

Let $\mathcal F$ be the explicitly declared feasible endpoint set of an isolated compound whose constituents are independent separated macroscopic systems, as defined in [[def-td-isolated-compound-feasible-set]]. For this route, adopt the physical criterion that any endpoint tuple the model classifies as a stable equilibrium under these fixed totals, retained partitions, and permitted exchanges satisfies

$$S_{\mathrm{tot}}(x^{\mathrm{eq}})=\max_{x\in\mathcal F}S_{\mathrm{tot}}(x),\qquad S_{\mathrm{tot}}(x):=\sum_{i=1}^{m}S_{c_i}(x_i),$$

Here $\max$ means that $x^{\mathrm{eq}}\in\mathcal F$ and $S_{\mathrm{tot}}(x^{\mathrm{eq}})\ge S_{\mathrm{tot}}(x)$ for every $x\in\mathcal F$, using maximum in the sense of [[def-max-min]]. The finite sum is as in [[def-finite-sum]], and the summands are those of the separated macroscopic constituents under [[post-td-concave-fundamental-entropy]]. Whenever the stable-equilibrium label is used, attainment is assumed: at least one maximizing endpoint lies in $\mathcal F$. If $\mathcal F$ is empty or the entropy supremum is not attained, this item supplies no equilibrium state.

“Global” refers to every endpoint in this exact $\mathcal F$, not just nearby states, states reachable by a restricted short-time dynamics, or states on a selected branch. A local maximum that is not global, or a long-lived preparation trapped by kinetic barriers, is not declared stable equilibrium by this postulate. No uniqueness or relaxation dynamics is assumed.

Fix a finite list of named subsystems $s_1,\ldots,s_m$, where $m\in\mathbb N$ and $m\ge1$ ([[def-natural-numbers]]), each having its own equilibrium state domain $D_{c_i}$ as defined in [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]]. Their separated endpoint state space is the Cartesian product ([[def-cartesian-product]])

$$\mathcal D:=D_{c_1}\times\cdots\times D_{c_m}.$$

An **isolated compound** is the system consisting of those subsystems and any named auxiliaries or work devices included inside a declared outer boundary, with no matter or energy transfer across that outer boundary during the admitted process, in the sense of [[def-td-system-and-permitted-exchanges]]. Transfers between constituents are internal to the compound. Its total energy and other extensive coordinates use the composition convention of [[post-td-bulk-additivity]]. The additive entropy sum applies only when the constituent split is admitted by [[post-td-concave-fundamental-entropy]] as a collection of independent separated macroscopic systems; an interacting compound outside that scope needs its own total-entropy model.

For specified totals and retained barriers, an **equilibrium feasible set** is the model-declared subset $\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal D$ of endpoint tuples satisfying those totals and exactly the exchange permissions in the declared protocol. Totals are imposed on the dimensioned coordinate maps $U_c,V_c,n_{c,j}$ of [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]], not by treating the dimensionless numerical coordinates as quantities with units. For example, if two constituents are in thermal contact through [[def-td-thermal-contact-constraints]] while their volumes and mole amounts remain fixed, $\mathcal F$ consists of the energy partitions $(x_A,x_B)$ with the prescribed total energy and those fixed volumes and amounts. Allowing volume or species exchange changes $\mathcal F$ only when the protocol explicitly permits that exchange; retained walls keep the corresponding coordinates fixed.

The set $\mathcal F$ may be empty, noncompact, or otherwise fail to contain an entropy-maximizing state. This definition imposes no existence, compactness, convexity, uniqueness, or attainment assumption.

Let $A$ and $B$ be two named subsystems with disjoint physical regions as in [[def-td-system-and-permitted-exchanges]], combined as a compound system $A\sqcup B$ inside a declared outer boundary. The model's admitted separated pairs form a specified subset $\mathcal C_{AB}\subseteq D_A\times D_B$ using [[def-subset-and-proper-subset]] and [[def-cartesian-product]]. For every pair $(x_A,x_B)\in\mathcal C_{AB}$, the composition map $\kappa_{AB}:\mathcal C_{AB}\to D_{A\sqcup B}$ is a function ([[def-function-space]]) adopted so the dimensioned coordinates of its output satisfy
$$U_{A\sqcup B}(\kappa_{AB}(x_A,x_B))=U_A(x_A)+U_B(x_B),\qquad V_{A\sqcup B}(\kappa_{AB}(x_A,x_B))=V_A(x_A)+V_B(x_B),\qquad n_{A\sqcup B,j}(\kappa_{AB}(x_A,x_B))=n_{A,j}(x_A)+n_{B,j}(x_B).$$
Here each coordinate function is the dimensioned map of [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]] for its material constitution, with SI units as in [[def-td-si-quantities]].

Here “extensive coordinates” means precisely the named coordinates declared additive by this postulate. Amount coordinates are aligned by species label; when a species is absent from one subsystem, its zero amount is in a separately declared composition boundary, not the positive-mole chart of [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]]. This is an idealized composition rule: cross-interface and long-range interaction energy is omitted from $U_{A\sqcup B}$, rather than asserted to vanish in nature. The postulate does not assert that every pair of subsystem states is physically admissible.

The framework's bulk family is a tagged family of material types. For each dimensionless scale $\lambda>0$ the model may designate a tag $c^{(\lambda)}$ and a subset $B_{c,\lambda}\subseteq D_c$ of states admitting a scaled copy, with inclusion as in [[def-subset-and-proper-subset]]. For $x=(\hat U,\hat V,\hat n_1,\ldots,\hat n_r)\in B_{c,\lambda}$, the scaling map is the function $\delta_\lambda:B_{c,\lambda}\to D_{c^{(\lambda)}}$ ([[def-function-space]]) given by $\delta_\lambda(x)=(\lambda\hat U,\lambda\hat V,\lambda\hat n_1,\ldots,\lambda\hat n_r)$. The tag matters: $c^{(\lambda)}$ is not silently identified with $c$. This postulate specifies the coordinate scaling model and energy additivity only; it does not postulate entropy additivity or exact scaling for every finite physical body.

This is an adopted physical composition rule, not a deduction from SI units or from the mathematics of Cartesian products.

For each admitted material constitution $c$, the model adopts a finite scalar function

$$S_c:D_c\longrightarrow\mathbb R\ \text{with values measured in }\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}},$$

on the equilibrium state domain $D_c$ of [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]]. This framework treats $S_c$ as primitive constitutive data: its existence and form are assumed, not derived from the word entropy, statistical mechanics, or experimental evidence.

On every specified convex region $C\subseteq D_c$ in the dimensionless coordinates of [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]], $S_c$ is continuous and concave, meaning that for all $x,y\in C$ and every $\alpha\in[0,1]$ ([[def-interval]]),

$$S_c((1-\alpha)x+\alpha y)\ge (1-\alpha)S_c(x)+\alpha S_c(y).$$

For independent separated macroscopic systems $A,B$ admitted by [[post-td-bulk-additivity]], entropy is additive under that postulate's composition map $\kappa_{AB}$:

$$S_{A\sqcup B}(\kappa_{AB}(x_A,x_B))=S_A(x_A)+S_B(x_B).$$

On each separately designated open, single-phase chart in the physical coordinates $(U,V,n_1,\ldots,n_r)$, assume the numerical representative of $S_c$ is $C^2$ in the sense of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]: its first and second coordinate partial derivatives exist and are continuous. The partial derivative $S_U$ at fixed $V,n_1,\ldots,n_r$ is the ordinary partial derivative in the $U$ coordinate, as in [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]], and is assumed finite and strictly positive. The numerical chart input uses $\hat U=U/(1\,\mathrm J)$; consequently $S_U=(1\,\mathrm J)^{-1}\partial S_c/\partial\hat U$ and has units $\mathrm{K^{-1}}$. The other physical coordinates are similarly represented using the fixed SI units of [[def-td-si-quantities]]. No differentiability, strict concavity, or positive $S_U$ is asserted outside those charts. This item does not itself define a thermometer calibration or claim a temperature law.

For the tagged bulk family with scaling maps $\delta_\lambda$ and domains $B_{c,\lambda}$ from [[post-td-bulk-additivity]], also adopt, for every admitted $\lambda>0$ and $x\in B_{c,\lambda}$,

$$S_{c^{(\lambda)}}(\delta_\lambda x)=\lambda S_c(x).$$

This is a bulk homogeneity assumption for tagged scaled systems, not exact finite-size scaling for every body. Let $A$ and $B$ be two named subsystems with disjoint physical regions as in [[def-td-system-and-permitted-exchanges]], combined as a compound system $A\sqcup B$ inside a declared outer boundary. The model's admitted separated pairs form a specified subset $\mathcal C_{AB}\subseteq D_A\times D_B$ using [[def-subset-and-proper-subset]] and [[def-cartesian-product]]. For every pair $(x_A,x_B)\in\mathcal C_{AB}$, the composition map $\kappa_{AB}:\mathcal C_{AB}\to D_{A\sqcup B}$ is a function ([[def-function-space]]) adopted so the dimensioned coordinates of its output satisfy
$$U_{A\sqcup B}(\kappa_{AB}(x_A,x_B))=U_A(x_A)+U_B(x_B),\qquad V_{A\sqcup B}(\kappa_{AB}(x_A,x_B))=V_A(x_A)+V_B(x_B),\qquad n_{A\sqcup B,j}(\kappa_{AB}(x_A,x_B))=n_{A,j}(x_A)+n_{B,j}(x_B).$$
Here each coordinate function is the dimensioned map of [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]] for its material constitution, with SI units as in [[def-td-si-quantities]].

Here “extensive coordinates” means precisely the named coordinates declared additive by this postulate. Amount coordinates are aligned by species label; when a species is absent from one subsystem, its zero amount is in a separately declared composition boundary, not the positive-mole chart of [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]]. This is an idealized composition rule: cross-interface and long-range interaction energy is omitted from $U_{A\sqcup B}$, rather than asserted to vanish in nature. The postulate does not assert that every pair of subsystem states is physically admissible.

The framework's bulk family is a tagged family of material types. For each dimensionless scale $\lambda>0$ the model may designate a tag $c^{(\lambda)}$ and a subset $B_{c,\lambda}\subseteq D_c$ of states admitting a scaled copy, with inclusion as in [[def-subset-and-proper-subset]]. For $x=(\hat U,\hat V,\hat n_1,\ldots,\hat n_r)\in B_{c,\lambda}$, the scaling map is the function $\delta_\lambda:B_{c,\lambda}\to D_{c^{(\lambda)}}$ ([[def-function-space]]) given by $\delta_\lambda(x)=(\lambda\hat U,\lambda\hat V,\lambda\hat n_1,\ldots,\lambda\hat n_r)$. The tag matters: $c^{(\lambda)}$ is not silently identified with $c$. This postulate specifies the coordinate scaling model and energy additivity only; it does not postulate entropy additivity or exact scaling for every finite physical body.

This is an adopted physical composition rule, not a deduction from SI units or from the mathematics of Cartesian products.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
For each admitted material constitution $c$, the model adopts a finite scalar function

$$S_c:D_c\longrightarrow\mathbb R\ \text{with values measured in }\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}},$$

on the equilibrium state domain $D_c$ of [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]]. This framework treats $S_c$ as primitive constitutive data: its existence and form are assumed, not derived from the word entropy, statistical mechanics, or experimental evidence.

On every specified convex region $C\subseteq D_c$ in the dimensionless coordinates of [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]], $S_c$ is continuous and concave, meaning that for all $x,y\in C$ and every $\alpha\in[0,1]$ ([[def-interval]]),

$$S_c((1-\alpha)x+\alpha y)\ge (1-\alpha)S_c(x)+\alpha S_c(y).$$

The domain assumptions are local to the material and region named; no unlisted coordinate tuple is presumed physically realizable. The input of $S_c$ is the represented state $\pi_c(e)$; when the function is written using physical coordinates $(U,V,n_1,\ldots,n_r)$, those coordinates mean the SI values whose dimensionless numerical tuple is $\pi_c(e)$. For independent separated macroscopic systems $A,B$ admitted by [[post-td-bulk-additivity]], entropy is additive under that postulate's composition map $\kappa_{AB}$:

$$S_{A\sqcup B}(\kappa_{AB}(x_A,x_B))=S_A(x_A)+S_B(x_B).$$

On each separately designated open, single-phase chart in the physical coordinates $(U,V,n_1,\ldots,n_r)$, assume the numerical representative of $S_c$ is $C^2$ in the sense of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]: its first and second coordinate partial derivatives exist and are continuous. The partial derivative $S_U$ at fixed $V,n_1,\ldots,n_r$ is the ordinary partial derivative in the $U$ coordinate, as in [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]], and is assumed finite and strictly positive. The numerical chart input uses $\hat U=U/(1\,\mathrm J)$; consequently $S_U=(1\,\mathrm J)^{-1}\partial S_c/\partial\hat U$ and has units $\mathrm{K^{-1}}$. The other physical coordinates are similarly represented using the fixed SI units of [[def-td-si-quantities]]. No differentiability, strict concavity, or positive $S_U$ is asserted outside those charts. This item does not itself define a thermometer calibration or claim a temperature law.

For the tagged bulk family with scaling maps $\delta_\lambda$ and domains $B_{c,\lambda}$ from [[post-td-bulk-additivity]], also adopt, for every admitted $\lambda>0$ and $x\in B_{c,\lambda}$,

$$S_{c^{(\lambda)}}(\delta_\lambda x)=\lambda S_c(x).$$

This is a bulk homogeneity assumption for tagged scaled systems, not exact finite-size scaling for every body. Lieb–Yngvason develop a different accessibility-based route in which entropy is represented from additional operational hypotheses; this framework does not claim that their derivation proves the present primitive entropy postulate.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Fix a system $s$ as in [[def-td-system-and-permitted-exchanges]]. A material constitution $c$ specifies a finite ordered list of named species $(\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_r)$, with $r\in\mathbb N$ ([[def-natural-numbers]]) and $r\ge1$, and the model parameters that identify the material. An equilibrium-preparation label in the set $E_c$ selects a single macrostate that the model designates as an equilibrium state for constitution $c$. The equilibrium designation is primitive model input here; it is not a dynamical equilibration theorem or a global-stability claim. For each admitted preparation, its mechanical model supplies a positive total mass and a defined center-of-mass velocity as in [[def-td-galilean-rest-frame]], so the allowed boost can select a center-of-mass rest chart in which its internal energy is recorded. A preparation for which these mechanical data are unavailable lies outside this framework. A statistical preparation that instead supplies a normalized probability measure on a declared measurable space is as in [[def-probability-measure]] and belongs to a separate statistical branch; it is an element of $E_c$ only if that model also assigns it a single equilibrium macrostate.

Each $e\in E_c$ is assigned a unique coordinate tuple $(U,V,n_1,\ldots,n_r)$, where $U$ is the adopted internal-energy coordinate in joules as in [[def-td-galilean-rest-frame]], $V>0$ is volume in cubic metres, and each $n_j>0$ is an amount in moles; the SI unit assignments are those of [[def-td-si-quantities]]. These are real-valued mole amounts in the bulk continuous chart, not integer particle counts. Define the dimensionless numerical coordinates $\hat U=U/(1\,\mathrm J)$, $\hat V=V/(1\,\mathrm{m^3})$, and $\hat n_j=n_j/(1\,\mathrm{mol})$. The representation map $\pi_c:E_c\to\mathbb R^{r+2}$ is a function as in [[def-function-space]], sends $e$ to $(\hat U,\hat V,\hat n_1,\ldots,\hat n_r)$, and the equilibrium state domain is its image $D_c:=\pi_c(E_c)\subseteq\mathbb R^{r+2}$ using inclusion as in [[def-subset-and-proper-subset]]. For $x=(\hat U,\hat V,\hat n_1,\ldots,\hat n_r)\in D_c$, write $U_c(x):=\hat U\,\mathrm J$, $V_c(x):=\hat V\,\mathrm{m^3}$, and $n_{c,j}(x):=\hat n_j\,\mathrm{mol}$ for its dimensioned coordinates. Preparation labels with the same coordinate tuple represent the same thermodynamic state in this framework. Statistical preparations that specify a probability law belong to a separate branch and are not used in this state-domain definition.

For fixed $n=(n_1,\ldots,n_r)$ in a chart used by the model, write $\Gamma_{c,n}=\{(\hat U,\hat V):(\hat U,\hat V,\hat n)\in D_c\}\subseteq\mathbb R^2$, with inclusion notation as in [[def-subset-and-proper-subset]]. This designated slice is a specified nonempty open convex subset. With the dimensionless Euclidean norm $\|\cdot\|_2$ of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]] (a norm by [[thm-cauchy-schwarz-and-the-euclidean-norm]]), openness means that every $z\in\Gamma_{c,n}$ has some $\epsilon>0$ for which $\{w\in\mathbb R^2:\|w-z\|_2<\epsilon\}\subseteq\Gamma_{c,n}$. Convexity means that $(1-t)z_0+tz_1\in\Gamma_{c,n}$ whenever $z_0,z_1\in\Gamma_{c,n}$ and $t\in[0,1]$, as in [[def-convex-subset-of-euclidean-space]]. Both properties are assumptions about the particular slice, not conclusions about every $D_c$; no coordinate tuple is presumed physically realizable merely because it lies in an ambient Euclidean space. A zero amount for an absent species belongs only to a separately specified boundary domain and is not in this positive-mole chart.

In a simple-compressible chart, volume $V$ is the only mechanical coordinate in the equilibrium representation; composition changes, fields, polarization, surface terms, and other mechanical coordinates require a separately declared state domain and exchange rules. No pressure or reversible-work formula follows from this definition.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
This framework uses the modern International System of Units (SI). A scalar quantity has a real numerical value with the stated unit; a vector quantity has a value in the stated real coordinate space with the stated component unit. The numerical coordinates used elsewhere on this page are divided by their displayed SI units before they are placed in a Euclidean coordinate space.

The model's energy coordinate $U$ and its process-transfer values $Q$ and $W_{\mathrm{on}}$ are scalar energies measured in joules (J). Volume $V$ is a scalar measured in cubic metres (m³); amount of substance $n_j$ for species $j$ is a scalar measured in moles (mol); and a particle count $N_j$, when separately used in a microscopic model, is dimensionless. Time $t$ is measured in seconds (s), mass $M$ in kilograms (kg), and a translational velocity $\mathbf v_{\mathrm{cm}}$ is a vector in $\mathbb R^3$ with components measured in metres per second (m/s). The physical meanings of $U,Q,W_{\mathrm{on}}$ are fixed by the state and process definitions, not by their units alone.

The relevant exact SI relations are

$$1\,\mathrm J=1\,\mathrm{kg\,m^2\,s^{-2}},\qquad 1\,\mathrm N=1\,\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-2}},\qquad 1\,\mathrm{Pa}=1\,\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}.$$

The kelvin (K) is the SI unit of thermodynamic temperature. The Boltzmann constant has the exact defining value $k_{\mathrm B}=1.380649\times10^{-23}\,\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$. The mole is the SI unit of amount of substance; the Avogadro constant has the exact defining value $N_{\mathrm A}=6.02214076\times10^{23}\,\mathrm{mol^{-1}}$. When a model uses particle counts, $n_j=N_j/N_{\mathrm A}$. The molar gas constant is derived as $R=N_{\mathrm A}k_{\mathrm B}=8.31446261815324\,\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$. This framework does not set $k_{\mathrm B}=1$. These SI definitions do not themselves introduce a thermodynamic temperature state function or entropy function.

Within the macroscopic framework, $(U,V,n_j)$ are adopted state coordinates. A quantity's status as primitive in this model is separate from whether its SI unit is a base or derived unit.

derivations.claim: Let tags be $\tau>0$, compose them by $\tau_A\oplus\tau_B=\tau_A+\tau_B$, and scale by $\tau^{(\lambda)}=\lambda\tau$. For constants $a>0$ in $\mathrm{K^{-1}}$, $b>0$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-3}}$, and $q>0$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, define on $D_\tau=\{(U,V,n):U,V,n>0\}$ the entropy $S_\tau(U,V,n)=aU+bV+q\tau$. By [F1] this is a positive-coordinate domain, and [F2] makes every term in the entropy dimensionally consistent. The function is finite, $C^2$, affine and hence concave, with $S_{\tau,U}=a>0$.

For two separated states, define the compound tag as $\tau_A+\tau_B$ and the composition map to add $U,V,n$. Then
$S_{\tau_A+\tau_B}(U_A+U_B,V_A+V_B,n_A+n_B)=S_{\tau_A}(U_A,V_A,n_A)+S_{\tau_B}(U_B,V_B,n_B)$,
so the model satisfies the stated coordinate and entropy additivity.
Under scaling, $S_{\lambda\tau}(\lambda U,\lambda V,\lambda n)=a\lambda U+b\lambda V+q\lambda\tau=\lambda S_\tau(U,V,n)$, so the tagged scaling relation in [A2] holds for every $\lambda>0$.

For the same fixed tag $\tau$, however, $S_\tau(2U,2V,2n)=2aU+2bV+q\tau$ whereas $2S_\tau(U,V,n)=2aU+2bV+2q\tau$. Since $q\tau>0$, these values differ. Thus tagged scaling plus the stated additivity does not imply fixed-tag homogeneity.
